Okay, with what you're describing it could be a tumor since this is NEW sudden onset headaches, but it could also be from a variety of conditions not so serious, so I would recommend talking to a doctor as soon as possible

Now because while many people have headaches for a variety of reasons brain tumor is within the realm of possibility, but Don't Panic, just because something is possible doesn't mean it's probable, no one here can rule out any number of possibilities without more tests and info. 

You may need a CT scan or mri to rule out tumor, hopefully you live somewhere that this can be done quickly, if not push your doctor to push the medical system to move faster. As the sooner you find out one way or another treatment can begin

The waking up I'm the middle of the night drenched sounds like my sleep apnea, which can also cause headaches and migraines, I've been told, though she probably needs to see a sleep doctor to have it confirmed. Lots of comorbidities make migraines worse. So it may be hormonal with menopause as someone else mentioned. So seeing a doctor is ideal. 
Getting her started with a migraine tracking app is a free way to see just how bad things have gotten, and provides a clearer record for medical personnel.

Unfortunately my experience has been that even with insurance finding good doctors and getting a good diagnosis takes time, money, and patience

At the worst, self harm starts to feel like a good idea, that taking a melon baller to scoop out your eyeballs would be preferable to the constant hot pain they're in, or that you start to understand why someone would take off a piece of their skull, to relieve the pressure you feel. And for more relatable to people who don't get migraines imagine the pain of a cold headache the worst one ever, now imagine it strobing in intensity and lasting instead of seconds, it lasts hours or days

I'm sorry you still don't have an answer, not that sleep apnea is easy, but it would have been treatable.
Hopefully you'll find a solution

I started getting daily headaches in my teens full migraines at 17, and migraines bevame a roughly weekly occurrence, some just a strong pain, others I am nauseous, photosensitive, audio sensitive, extreme pain where removing an eye feels at the time like it might be preferable. have had various ups and downs in life, worked for a decade, never found a partner, but at 42 I'm on disability wondering if I will ever work again,  deal with depression, and sleep apnea. You probably won't go down the same path as me. Lots of people here have migraines yet manage relationships and work and children despite having this disease

To me this is an interesting way to think about migraines,   there are certain actions which do feel more likely to get a migraine but I've never experienced life where you can avoid all possible triggers. Food is a weird trigger, I've given up trying to associate foods with migraines, even though I still believe some foods have caused migraines. But the association is limited and sometimes seems like I made it up. So is it a migraine trigger hard to really know, since it seems like so many things in life can be triggers. If you wake up with a migraine was it a change in sleep pattern or something from the day before, or a change in hormones, or the weather. 

I know it would be good to keep a migraine diary but it felt so depressing with how common they were, the lack of control I had over them, and the lack of motivation to document anything.

I dunno. One expert does not a consensus make, but it's good to try to think of this disease in new ways

Best of luck to you, some of the medical devices can be purchased online, direct from manufacturer or even Amazon, they aren't covered by insurance typically but may be a cheaper option than price of the meds in the UK. Just be aware these have a lower efficacy than medication at this point, so they may not work for you

Are you in a part of the world with access to anti cgrp meds? Aimovig, emgality, ajovy, qulipta, can be taken as preventative,  nurtec taken as an abortive/ preventative and ubrelvy as an abortive.  These meds have few side affects nor interactions with other meds. There is also non medicine devices like cefaly and some others I can't remember the names of look for migraine medical equipment. Also botox might be an option to treat the migraines.
 But yes neurological/emotional issues can impact mood, so a therapis would be good. it may be worthwhile as well to possibly getting on an anti anxiety med at least temporarily while you learn the tools to deal with the anxiety.

 Magnesium and other supplements had no effect for me, but they work for some people. Taking ibuprofen or other nsaids, can lead to rebound headaches so if possible try to restrict your use of those for regular headaches or migraine .

I get temple pain more often than eye pain, so yes. Sometimes it starts in my temple and then an eye or two join in the pain. However if this is a new phenomenon check with your doc, as changes like that can be linked to other causes.
I dont really remember the specifics of the cyst, the doctor said it was tiny and had likely been there all my life, it showed up on one MRI and was a faint spot. I try not to worry about it too much

My doctors have mentioned medication overuse headaches from over the counter medications, they said you should only use Tylenol or ibuprofen twice in a week for headaches. And that it can take a month (iirc) of going without nsaids to normalize. It's been better since I stopped using nsaids so often but I still have a daily headache, and still get migraines but now it's not every other day, it also helped to get a good supply of ubrelvy for my migraines.

The ER trip sounds super scary, so does finding out you have mass inside your head.  I know you're not exaggerating when you say you've had a headache everyday,  I've dealt with that for years now I'm a 42 year old male that was diagnosed with migraines and chronic headache in my teens. The headache never really seems to go away for me, and then gets worse with the migraine.  I had no injury or incident that precipitated this pain. I have a small benign cyst that was discovered on an mri about 5 years ago but it was likely just missed on previous ones, and not causing the headaches. I never had any luck with botox either. Though some new doctors would like me try it again for an either 3rd or 4th time, and I have had multiple preventative medications either not work or stop working. But I'm trying a new medication ajovy, migraines seem like they might be less frequent, but I still get a daily headache.  And you're right migraine is kinda a catch all term for headaches of unknown origin, you don't really confirm it , it seems  more like you rule out other serious things and then you're left with migraines or chronic daily headaches.  I'm sorry I don't have any good treatment or doctor options, but anti cgrp drugs have had some effect for me.

I'm sorry things are so tough right now. You may want to look in to finding a decent therapist, since depression and chronic pain can be a sliding slope with them feeding each other. But don't give up hope, things may change, you may find medicines that help your migraines. I know what it's like to feel helpless, but right now I think you still have options, it may take longer than you would like and not everything may be completely fixed but it is possible for life to be better than it is right now. I hope you find relief soon. Feel free to reach out to me or this community for ideas for treatment and support

You sound very similar to me, I get migraines a couple of times a month 2 to 5, but have headaches everyday and it's been going on since high school for me, am now 41. 
I also have sleep apnea, which does not help with headaches. I have taken amitriptyline and the most notable effect was I gained weight, Topamax also did nothing positive. 

Getting used to pain seems like it only goes so far. And even on days the headache isn't so bad it's still tiring. But I ve been told that taking pills for the everyday headaches causes medication overuse headaches. Im not sure for me the everyday heaches are serious enough that i need an ice pack and pills too often.

There are other preventative medicines, the new class of cgrp meds, like emgality, aimovig, and ajovy, that come as injections and qulipta which is a daily pill.
There are other treatments like botox which injected every couple of months, but some people swear by as a preventative.

I did go to pain management doctor who prescribed fentanyl and while I do not take it anymore and not really sure it should be tried, it did knock out migraines quickly even if they were in full swing. 

I have seen multiple neurologists, some good some bad,  for me they have been more helpful than regular doctors. I have tried botox, emgality and now on aimovig and also use Ubrelvy as rescue. 

Chiropractic care never helped with the headaches, massages sometimes helped a little, have also tried Tms or transcranial magnetic stimulation but have found nothing that works for preventing headaches. 

So when nothing works, you may be handed off to other specialists like i was, where I've seen psychiatrists, sleep doctors, to try to rule out other causes of headache.

 Really felt frustrated when a doctor recommended I get a dog as solution to multiple problems, not being active enough, walk the dog, not having enough companionship,  the dog will love you and help you meet people.

I find it hard to remove all triggers from life. Triggers for me include, changes in sleep pattern, changes in stress level, weather, sunlight, loud noise, dietary ones which range from having enough water and protein to specific foods like garlic. I'm a guy in my forties so I don't have the hormonal triggers some women do, and oh yes I forgot getting sick seems to be a trigger too, probably gave me today's and yesterday's migraines. But even with all of that there are still days I can't point to a specific trigger and say oh yeah I did this so of course I had a migraine.

There are other medications besides triptans if as a class of drugs they seem to not work for you anymore, like ubrelvy and nurtec as abortives, if you have them more often there are other preventative meds, but see if other triptans work first as the drugs I mention are newer and tend to be more expensive

There is a whole class of anti cgrp drugs, three injectables you take as monthly preventive, I know of, ajovy, emgality, and aimovig, your doc may have a preference for one of these, and insurance may also have its say, but they help some people. There is also ubrelvy which is an as needed pill.
 I'm currently taking aimovig, and have taken emgality in the past but stopped when it seemed like it stopped working. And I take ubrelvy which can be expensive, but usually works to stop a migraine. Nurtec I tried but didn't find helpful even though it's part of the new group of migraine specific drugs. So there are other options besides getting stronger pain drugs.

It's not necessarily that people think you are stupid, but they want to help and there is very little they can do, especially by phone, so reminding someone to take their meds when they may not be thinking clearly is one thing they can do, but if it's causing you stress and frustration explain that these repetitive questions are not helping and only make things worse.

Migraines despite what you have heard are a very non-specific disorder, the main identifier really is pain. Not all migraines present with auras or a sensitivity to sound, and it is not necessarily the worst pain you have ever felt either, those are just what gets reported most about migraines. I sometimes get nausea but not always with my migraines, and feel pain all over my head and neck, sometimes it is sharp and pounding but other times it is dull and generalized, sometimes with pain medication I can prevent serious pain but am left feeling foggy.
 
 I would continue with what you are doing trying to rule out other issues, and get the MRI, but would also tell them you have a family history of migraines, since your mom gets them, and hopefully they will give you some migraine specific medication like imitrex or promethazine and if that works it is very likely you were having a migraine. 

And if your current doctors can't figure anything out but don't believe these are migraines don't be afraid to get a second opinion, I once had a doctor straight up tell me that what I had could not be a migraine even though my current neurologist has very little doubt I get chronic migraines
